subject: Question on Scalar Invariance Testing Accounting for Age Effects

messages.author: 60cfdaab93c622cc
messages.subject: Question on Scalar Invariance Testing Accounting for Age Effects
parts:
Dear all,

I am using a longitudinal CFA to model a latent construct (small vessel disease - SVD) that is measured by 3 MRI indicators. My initial goal is to test the measurement invariance of that model over two time points (baseline and follow-up). Even though the configural and metric invariance models hold, the scalar invariance model is rejected. My suspicion is that this is due to factors other than SVD influencing the indicators over time. The first one that comes to mind is age (also, the age effect might be different for each indicator, and might also be different across the two time points).

In an attempt to account for that age effect, I incorporated a set of regressions in the model, where I basically regress each indicator on age. Then, the fit of the scalar invariance model improves significantly.

This, in my mind, is a similar approach of using residuals to partial out the age effect from each MRI indicator, but I also incorporate these regressions in the model so the overall fit can be tested.

I would really appreciate your input on whether this approach is correct or testing scalar invariance using this model is not valid for some reason.

Thank you in advance!

This is the parametrization I'm using (I'm including only the scalar invariance model for brevity):

model <-('
ind1_t1 ~ age.1
ind1_t2 ~ age.2
ind2_t1 ~ age.1
ind2_t2 ~ age.2
ind3_t1 ~ age.1
ind3_t2 ~ age.2

age.1 ~~ age.2

# Measurement model for svd in time 1
 svd_1 =~ 1*ind1_t1 + l2*ind2_t1 + l3*ind3_t1

# Measurement model for svd in time 2
 svd_2 =~ 1*ind1_t2 + l2*ind2_t2 + l3*ind3_t2

# Mean structure specification
ind1_t1 ~ i1*1
ind2_t1 ~ i2*1
ind3_t1 ~ i3*1
ind1_t2 ~ i1*1
ind2_t2 ~ i2*1
ind3_t2 ~ i3*1

# Residual covariances
ind1_t1  ~~  ind1_t2
ind2_t1  ~~  ind2_t2
ind3_t1  ~~  ind3_t2

# Latent variable means
svd_1 ~ 0*1
svd_2 ~ 1')

fit <- lavaan::sem(model, data = dat, estimator = "MLR")

parts: I would consider regressing the latent variables on age instead of the measured variables. That will also test for age invariance and as a bonus, save you some degrees of freedom.

parts:
Dear Jeremy,

Thanks a lot for your response. I have indeed considered this approach, the only issue is that it doesn't account for the fact that the age effect might not be homogenous across MRI indicators (some are known to be affected more by/be more sensitive to brain aging than others).

Best wishes,
Sokratis
